course_summary:
ISEN 625 | Simulation Methods and Applications | Fall 2026
Instructor: Amarnath Banerjee | banerjee@tamu.edu
Meets: Online, no scheduled meetings
Grading: Exam 1 [18 points], Exam 2 [18 points], Lab Exam 1 [22 points], Lab Exam 2 [22 points], Lab assignments [12 points], Quizzes [8 points] — A: 90-100%, B: 80-89.9%, C: 70-79.9%, D: 60-69.9%, F: below 60%
Topics: KN method, OptQuest, Agent Based Simulation, mixed model simulation, fluid flows combined with discrete event simulation, pull (Kanban) system, Goodness of Fit tests, Monte Carlo Simulation, non-stationary arrival process, discrete event (process-oriented) simulation modeling, random variate generation techniques, random number generation tests, user defined statistics, custom run setup, relational tables, separation of data from model, reliability logic, Task Sequences, Simio constructs, queueing theory, basic queueing models, two different types of systems, properties of output data, system comparison, non-terminating system analysis, data fitting, developing confidence intervals, probability statements, expectations, PDF's, PMF's, CDF's, single variable distributions, joint probabilities distributions, calculus-based probability, Simulation-Based Optimization, Variance Reduction Technique, ranking and selection, Verification, Validation, Input Analysis, Output Analysis, simulation data preparation, analysis of simulation output, random numbers, random variates, lists, sequences, transporters, work schedule, function, counting, branching, plots, interpreting results, processes, modeling, simulation, statistics, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, computer programming
Tools: Simio, Canvas
Prerequisites: STAT 212 or STAT 601, STAT 630, ISEN 609, STAT 211, knowledge of computer programming, calculus-based probability and statistics, distributions (single variable and joint probabilities), PDF's, PMF's, CDF's, probability statements, expectations, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing
